title: HookConfig
description: A hooks file (FR-197, ADR-068, docs/08 §4.1): managed policy, the user hooks.json, a trusted project's .nova/hooks.json, or a plugin's hooks file. A hook runs sandboxed and only while its content hash equals the hash the user trusted. It can block, add context, answer an eligible ask, or request one continuation at stop; it never overrides built-in safety, managed policy, a deny or a handoff.

matcher.description: Glob(s) over the event's matcher subject (tool name, role, start reason or compaction trigger). Absent = every occurrence.

failClosed.description: On error or timeout, block the prompt (prompt.submit) instead of having no effect. tool.pre and permission.request hooks always fail closed: a failed or timed-out run blocks the call or denies the request whatever this says.

command.description: Fixed argv; no shell. Runs in the session sandbox under its permission profile.

network.description: Hosts the hook may reach; absent = network off. Plugin hooks stay within the plugin's network permissions.

tool.description: Canonical MCP tool name; the call passes the policy engine with origin hook. M8 (ADR-097 D3): an SDK hook's stored handler names its extension's hook tool, ext:<extensionId>/hooks/<hookId>, which the extension's worker answers.

result.description: A handler's answer (stdout JSON for command handlers, the tool result for mcp_tool). Empty output means no opinion.

decision.description: permission.request only, and only for an ask raised by a user rule or a per-tool default.

context.description: Added as a hook_prompt item; spilled to a file above 2,500 tokens. Untrusted.

continue.description: stop only: text for one continuation turn within the run budget.

trustRecord.description: Stored by the Hub, never in the hooks file (docs/06 hook table).
